scoreNote: Strong-adequate (4.5): grants that youth trends reveal a culture's direction, then argues they are only one part of the whole; two developed examples with analysis, controlled prose on a memorable First and Second skeleton.

sentences.text: The music, fashion, and slang of young people often seem to capture the spirit of an age.
Some people argue that the most effective way to understand contemporary culture is to analyse the trends of its youth.
I agree that youth culture reveals a great deal, but I do not believe it is the only or the best way to understand a society.

sections.role: Body 1 — Why youth trends reveal much

sentences.text: First, the trends of young people often show where a culture is heading.
Because the young adopt new ideas quickly, their habits hint at the future of the whole society.
For example, the way teenagers embraced the internet early showed how deeply technology would reshape daily life.
This shows that watching youth trends can reveal changes long before they spread to everyone else.
Young people also tend to express the hopes and frustrations of their time openly and honestly.
Their music and art often capture feelings that older generations are slower to admit.
To this extent, studying the young really does illuminate a culture.

sections.role: Body 2 — Why they are not the whole picture

sentences.text: Second, however, youth trends alone cannot reveal the whole of a culture.
A society is also shaped by its families, workers, leaders, and long-standing traditions.
Consider how a country's laws, religions, and history shape daily life far more than any passing teenage fashion.
Such forces show that much of a culture lies well beyond the world of the young.
Many youth trends, moreover, fade quickly and never truly represent the wider society.
Focusing only on the young would ignore the values and habits of everyone else.
A full understanding of culture, then, must look well beyond its youth.
In conclusion, the trends of young people offer real and valuable clues about a culture.
But they form only one part of a society shaped by many groups and traditions.
We understand a culture best by studying its youth alongside everyone and everything else.
